name: timeline
purpose: Shows an activity or event history: items with a time (an exact instant or an all-day date), a title, a description, an icon or avatar, a status tone shown by icon and word, and keyboard-reachable actions. Vertical or horizontal, items on one side or alternating, grouped by day in the configured timezone with business-calendar names for holidays and non-working days, relative or absolute times, and older items collapsed behind 'Show N older' or loaded on demand with loading, error, and retry states.
whenToUse: Activity history of a record: document changes, approvals, employee profile events.
Order or case tracking with a status per step in time.
A horizontal milestone overview, such as a project or onboarding plan.
whenNotToUse: Step-by-step task flows the user moves through: use Stepper.
Scheduling or durations on a time axis: use Gantt or Scheduler.
responsive: Vertical timelines are fluid and wrap text; alternate timelines keep both sides at equal width; horizontal timelines scroll in a focusable region with items of 14rem.
rtl: The line, markers, and alternate sides mirror; horizontal timelines run from the right.
theme: Component tokens timeline-line-color (color-border-strong), timeline-marker-size (icon-size-md), and timeline-marker-neutral, -info, -success, -warning, -error (tone foregrounds), every marker 3:1 against color-surface in the contrast gate. Forced colors use CanvasText on Canvas.
timezone: Instants are grouped and formatted in the configured timezone (common config or the timezone option); PlainDate items are all-day and never shift. Day headings name holidays and non-working days from a business calendar.
security: Titles, descriptions, status words, and action labels are rendered with textContent; item hrefs are limited to http(s) and relative URLs, avatar sources to safe image URLs; invalid values throw before rendering.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry; loadMore is host code.

budgets.metric: Timeline.create with 1,000 items grouped by day

performance.testedScale: Up to 10,000 items in memory; use initialVisible or loadMore to keep the DOM to a few hundred items.

limitations: Not virtualized: keep the rendered items to a few hundred with initialVisible or loadMore.
Relative times are computed at render; call update({ now }) to refresh them.
The alternate layout applies to vertical timelines only.
unsupported: Rich text (HTML) in titles or descriptions.
Durations or overlapping ranges on a time axis (use Gantt).
antiPatterns: Showing status by color alone: give each item a tone or a status word.
Rendering thousands of items at once instead of collapsing older ones.
